fields.description:
## Context

Discovered while root-causing `dewy-rotatable-tarsier` (d240). It is NOT that bug's root cause —
that is sync MCP tool bodies blocking the event loop — but it is a real, separate defect surfaced
by the same investigation, so it is filed rather than folded in.

## The defect

`/health` returning 200 does not establish that the container can serve an MCP request, yet it is
the ONLY thing the blue-green cutover waits for.

- `/health` is a FastMCP `custom_route` registered DELIBERATELY outside `RequireAuthMiddleware` and
  outside the DNS-rebinding transport-security guard (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:210-224`), so a 200
  exercises none of: the auth middleware, the transport-security host/origin guard,
  `ProxyAuthMiddleware`, the StreamableHTTP session manager, or the MCP handshake.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:794-798` polls `GET http://127.0.0.1:<newport>/health` until 200 and
  then flips the nginx upstream (`autodeploy.sh:835`). **The deploy path never issues a single
  `/mcp` request.** A container is promoted to live traffic having never proven it can serve one.

Measured on the box (2026-08-28): container started 20:21:23.80, uvicorn bound 20:21:29.00, first
`/health` 200 at 20:21:29.87, cutover logged at 20:21:30, and the container did not serve its first
`/mcp` request until **20:22:24** — 54 seconds after it was declared healthy and put in front of
traffic.

## Why it matters

A container whose `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` does not admit the public hostname answers
`/health` 200 while returning **421 Invalid Host header** to every real request. Verified
in-process: driving an `initialize` through the session manager with a Host outside the allowlist
returns 421 in under a millisecond, while `/health` on the same server returns 200. The deploy would
promote that container and log "mcp redeployed + healthy". The same is true of an auth
misconfiguration.

Related: during the 5.5-7.5 s of Python process startup BEFORE uvicorn binds (measured across three
deploys: 5.20 s / 7.54 s / 5.49 s), the published host port is ALREADY bound by docker-proxy, so an
arriving connection is accepted and then hangs or is reset rather than being refused. Blue-green
shields autodeploy-driven deploys from that window, but `--restart always` (`autodeploy.sh:377`)
does not: a container that crashes restarts in place on the port nginx is currently pointing at,
with no health gate involved at all.

## This is a known class in this repo

`store_status`'s docstring (`_mcp_health.py:118-129`) and its pinning test
(`tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py`) record that `/health` used to report only
`in_flight`, so a container with NO ticket store passed both the container HEALTHCHECK and the
blue-green readiness gate, and a deployed server answered every tracker query as though the store
were empty for weeks (bugs `kilted-nuclear-bronco` / `mobile-groovy-badger`). The established
invariant is that `/health` must carry enough signal for the readiness gate to be meaningful. The
MCP request path — the only thing the container exists to serve — is still unrepresented in it.

## Approach

Drive one real `initialize` through this server's own `StreamableHTTPSessionManager` inside the
ASGI lifespan, after the session manager is running and before Starlette answers
`lifespan.startup.complete`, and publish the outcome as a `handshake` object on `/health` beside
`in_flight` and `store`. Uvicorn does not accept a connection until lifespan startup completes
(`Router.lifespan` sends `lifespan.startup.complete` only after the lifespan context has been
entered — `starlette/routing.py`), so a later `/health` 200 proves BY CONSTRUCTION that this
container has already served an MCP handshake. That is why the handshake goes in the lifespan
rather than in a background task or behind a lazily-evaluated `/health` field: only the lifespan
ordering makes "healthy" imply "has served one".

Two properties are required and they pull against each other; both are designed for explicitly.

**Conclusive.** The probe calls `mcp.session_manager.handle_request(scope, receive, send)` — the
same entry point the `/mcp` route serves through (`StreamableHTTPASGIApp(self._session_manager)`,
`mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py:970`). A 200 therefore cannot be produced unless the DNS-rebinding
transport-security guard admitted the Host, `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` parsed the body, the
session manager's task group started a server task, and `Server.run` answered the `initialize`
JSON-RPC request. Confirmed by a throwaway in-process probe against a `FastMCP` built exactly as
`build_server` builds it: 200 in 3.0 ms with an admitting allowlist, 421 ("Invalid Host header")
in 2.1 ms with a non-admitting one. **Stated boundary:** the drive does NOT traverse
`RequireAuthMiddleware`/`ProxyAuthMiddleware`, because the server has no client credential to
present to itself and an auth-enabled boot would then always report failure; the handshake proves
the transport + protocol path, not the auth configuration. `/health` is unchanged in that respect.

**Bounded.** The drive runs under `anyio.fail_after(budget)` with a module constant
`DEFAULT_HANDSHAKE_BUDGET_SECONDS = 10`, and the whole call is wrapped so that a `TimeoutError`,
any `Exception`, or a non-200 status becomes a reported failure record rather than a raise —
boot then continues and uvicorn serves. The timeout scope and the clock are INJECTED parameters
(`fail_after=anyio.fail_after`, `monotonic=time.monotonic`), the same seam
`drain_then_exit(..., sleep=, monotonic=)` already uses in this module (`_mcp_health.py`), so the
bound is provable in a unit test with a fake clock instead of by sleeping.

**Probe Host selection** (`select_probe_host`) is a total function of the server's own
`TransportSecuritySettings` plus its bind: (1) the first `allowed_hosts` entry that is a literal
host (no `*`) — on the box that is `rebar.solutions.navateam.com`
(`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:359`), i.e. what real traffic actually carries; (2) else the
first `host:*` port-wildcard entry materialized as `host:<bind port>`, since the guard matches
that form (`mcp/server/transport_security.py`, `_validate_host` wildcard branch); (3) else the
bind address with `0.0.0.0`/`::` normalized to `127.0.0.1`. A server whose allowlist admits
nothing usable (empty, or only unsupported wildcard forms such as `*.example.com`, which
`_validate_host` can never match) therefore falls through to (3) and gets a 421 from its own
guard — which is the AC-2 case, reported with the refusing status rather than as ready. Drawing
the probe Host from the allowlist rather than always from the bind is deliberate: the box binds
`0.0.0.0:8091` (`docker-compose.yml:337`) and allows only the public hostname, so a
bind-addressed probe would report a correctly configured production container as failed.

The deploy gate is closed the same way the store gate was (`autodeploy.sh` step 5b): after
`/health` returns 200, refuse to flip the nginx upstream when `handshake.ok` is present and
false. Absent field ⇒ promote (mixed-version safety, exactly as the `store` gate treats an older
container).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` — `select_probe_host`, the ASGI `initialize` drive, the bounded
  never-raising `run_startup_handshake`, `install_startup_handshake` (wraps
  `app.router.lifespan_context`, unwrapping the `ProxyAuthMiddleware` wrapper when present), the
  `handshake` field on `/health`, and the call from `run_http_with_grace` after
  `mcp.streamable_http_app()`. Module is 372 LOC today; the addition keeps it well under the
  800-LOC cap.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_startup_handshake.py` — new unit tests (below).
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — readiness gate on `handshake.ok`, mirroring step 5b.
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` — deploy-gate tests on the existing
  `mcp_box` harness, which already stubs `/health` bodies per port.

No new config key: the budget is a module constant, for the reason the module docstring already
records for `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS` (a config key would ripple into `MCP_ENV_VARS` /
`server.json` / the env-var docs generators).

## Testing

Every assertion is anchored: each test proves the handshake actually RAN (a recorded drive
count, or the `handshake` record's presence) before asserting its outcome — an assertion that
would pass when the handshake never ran is this bug restated.

- **Positive (real path).** A `FastMCP` built with a literal admitting allowlist: enter the
  lifespan, assert the recorded `handshake` is `{"ok": true, "status": 200}` with a numeric
  `elapsed_ms` — and assert the drive counter incremented, so a no-op cannot pass.
- **Negative (misconfigured server).** Same server with `allowed_hosts=["*.example.com"]` (a form
  the guard can never match): assert `ok is False` and `status == 421`, i.e. the refusing status,
  and that `/health` reports it rather than reporting ready.
- **Bounded, injected clock.** A drive that never returns, with an injected `fail_after` driven
  by an injected fake clock: assert the call RETURNS (does not raise), reports
  `ok is False` with `error` naming the timeout and the budget, and that the test does no real
  sleeping.
- **Never raises.** A drive that raises `RuntimeError("boom")`: assert the record is a failure
  carrying the message and that boot continues (the lifespan context still yields).
- **Ordering (AC 4).** Drive the wrapped app's lifespan through the raw ASGI protocol and assert
  the recorded handshake exists BEFORE `lifespan.startup.complete` is sent.
- **`select_probe_host`.** Literal-first, `host:*` materialization, and bind fallback with
  `0.0.0.0` → `127.0.0.1`.
- **Deploy gate.** Three tests on the `mcp_box` harness: a `handshake.ok=false` body must log
  `mcp-handshake-failed`, leave the old include byte-identical, not reload nginx, and remove the
  refused container; a `handshake.ok=true` body must still promote; a body with no `handshake`
  key must still promote.
- **Mutation check.** Each production edit is reverted individually and the targeted test must
  fail (checked by return code, with each seed confirmed applied).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A correctly configured server reports a successful startup handshake on `/health`:
      `test_correctly_configured_server_reports_a_successful_handshake` asserts the drive counter
      incremented and the record is `{"ok": True, "status": 200}`.
- [ ] A server whose transport-security host allowlist does not admit its own probe reports the
      handshake as failed with the refusing status, instead of reporting ready:
      `test_unadmitted_probe_host_is_reported_as_failed_with_421` asserts `ok is False` and
      `status == 421`.
- [ ] The handshake never raises and never hangs: `test_a_hanging_drive_is_bounded_by_the_budget`
      (injected clock, no real sleep) and `test_a_raising_drive_is_reported_not_propagated` both
      assert the call returns a failure record and the lifespan still yields.
- [ ] The handshake completes inside the ASGI lifespan, before uvicorn accepts its first
      connection: `test_handshake_is_recorded_before_lifespan_startup_complete` drives the raw
      ASGI lifespan protocol and asserts the record exists before `lifespan.startup.complete`.
- [ ] The blue-green cutover refuses to promote a container reporting a failed handshake:
      `test_failed_handshake_container_is_not_promoted` asserts `mcp-handshake-failed` is logged,
      the upstream include is byte-identical, nginx is not reloaded, and the container is removed;
      `test_container_with_no_handshake_field_still_promotes` pins mixed-version safety.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the affected test modules pass in-session (exit 0), and
      each production edit reverted individually makes its targeted test fail (return code
      checked).
